INCIDENT REPORT — IR-2026-041
Service: Atlas Search API. Window: 02:14-03:47 UTC, August 12.
Summary: Elevated error rates (peaking at 38% of requests) affected the Atlas Search API for 93 minutes. The root cause was a configuration change that set the cache TTL to 0 seconds, causing every query to hit the primary database and exhaust its connection pool. The on-call engineer rolled back the change at 03:41; error rates returned to baseline within 6 minutes. Approximately 41,000 requests failed. No data was lost. Action items: (1) add a config-validation gate to the deploy pipeline, (2) raise the connection-pool alarm threshold sensitivity, (3) schedule a blameless retro for August 18.

ABSTRACT — Journal of Coastal Ecology (fictional)
We monitored nesting success of the dune lark (Calendulauda dunensis) across 14 sites on the Alderney coast over three breeding seasons. Sites with restored marram grass cover showed a mean nesting success of 61%, compared with 34% at unrestored sites. Predation by gulls accounted for 58% of nest failures overall, but only 29% at restored sites, suggesting vegetation cover primarily reduces predation rather than improving food availability. Trail camera data indicated human disturbance within 50 m of nests reduced fledging rates by roughly a third regardless of site restoration. We recommend pairing vegetation restoration with seasonal 50 m buffer zones around active colonies.

--- TEXT ---
SPEC EXCERPT — Draft v0.3, 'Beacon' presence protocol
A Beacon node announces itself every 30 seconds over multicast group 239.44.10.9, port 8771. An announcement contains the node ID (16 bytes), a monotonically increasing epoch counter, and a capability bitmask. A node is considered live by peers if an announcement arrives within 90 seconds of the previous one (three missed intervals). On epoch rollover (2^31), nodes must rejoin with epoch 1 and a new random session salt. Announcements are not encrypted in v0.3; deployments on untrusted networks should use the optional HMAC trailer defined in section 6. Nodes with the relay bit set must forward announcements to directly connected subnets within 500 ms.
